cases.title: scheduled: the request, what it suspends, the tombstone export, the limits, the audit export's key

expect.stdout:
Deletion of acme scheduled.
Deletion del_1 of acme: scheduled 2026-11-19T10:00:00.000Z by Ada.
It runs no earlier than 2100-01-01T00:00:00.000Z.
It waits for another admin's approval: varlatch org delete acme --approve del_1
acme is frozen until then: changes are refused, reads still work, so a last copy can be made.
Any admin can cancel it until it runs: varlatch org delete acme --cancel del_1
Machine identities and webhooks are suspended and Sync Targets paused; pending invitations were revoked. When it runs, every membership ends, machines are retired, values are erased and the organization's key is destroyed.
After it runs, the people who can then read org_acme's audit log export it with: varlatch audit export --deleted-org org_acme
Deletion covers this installation's live database. It does not reach:
  PostgreSQL's old row versions and write-ahead log, its replicas and snapshots of its volume, which keep the data for a while;
  requests already authorized: the server may still hold their keys or values in memory, and one in flight when the deletion runs may still complete;
  backups taken before it completes: they keep the data until their retention removes them, and restoring one brings it back;
  values already pushed to platforms: they stay there;
  values revealed, downloaded or exported: they stay wherever they were copied. Rotate them at their provider to make old copies useless.
A GitHub App stays as it is on GitHub: uninstall it or delete it there, and revoke copies of its private key. Installation tokens already issued stay valid until they expire.
The audit export's key stays readable by this installation for up to 30 days after deletion, to deliver the final audit events. Nothing else does.
